Done. The export is written to `out/T3/` and passed on the first execution.

**What I did**

- Wrote `out/T3/solution.py` using plain torch and safetensors. It reads the input, casts the 48 projection matrices matched by an anchored regex to bfloat16, drops the 12 causal-mask buffers, and passes every other tensor through unchanged.
- The script enforces the required checks before writing: 48 bfloat16 tensors, `h.0.attn.c_attn.weight` is bfloat16, `wte.weight` is float32, 148 tensors total. It also checks names and shapes are unchanged and float32 values are bit-identical.
- Sharding is greedy in sorted key order with a 64 MiB budget. The embedding matrix exceeds the budget and is stored alone in its own shard.

**Result**

| Shard | Tensors | Tensor bytes |
|---|---|---|
| model-00001-of-00004 | 59 | 66,259,968 |
| model-00002-of-00004 | 58 | 66,256,896 |
| model-00003-of-00004 | 30 | 40,983,552 |
| model-00004-of-00004 | 1 | 154,389,504 |

An independent re-read of the shards confirmed the index covers all 148 tensors, every bfloat16 tensor equals the source cast with round-to-nearest-even, and every float32 tensor is bit-identical to the input.

The self-report is in `out/T3/REPORT.md`. It notes one open assumption: the task does not fix shard file names or packing order, so I used the HuggingFace naming convention and sorted-key greedy packing.
